summary: All five criteria are met. npm test passes 120 of 120 (the new tests/bash-prose.test.mjs passes 13 of 13 on its own), and npm run check passes (syntax ok, openspec validate 11 of 11). Cat and tee heredocs that only write a file are dropped from the judged text, heredocs fed to a shell or interpreter stay scanned, the push deny pattern and push rule are confined to one line, the five test cases exist, and docs/rules.md has the row. One major behavior risk remains: a body that writes a denied command to a file is allowed in its own call, and a later call that runs that file (bash run.sh) is also allowed, because the file's contents are never judged across calls. This is the trade-off the goal accepts, so it does not block, but the rules row does not state the cross-call limit.

findings.issue: A cat or tee heredoc body that writes a denied command to a file is allowed in its own call, and a later call that runs the file is also allowed, so the deny patterns never see the command that runs.
findings.suggestion: State the cross-call limit in the docs/rules.md row, or judge a later bash invocation of a file that a heredoc wrote in the same session.
